KR.read: Korea's fragrances segment data consists solely of export figures; no domestic retail or production market-size figure is present. The most recent export value is US$0.06bn (2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH confidence, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald). A separate HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade figure puts 2024 HS 3303 exports to the world at US$0.039471bn - a different source and period than the MFDS total, so the two should not be read as one continuous series. Of that 2024 world-export figure, only US$6,000 (0.000006bn) went to India, a [CORRIDOR]-tagged flow that is a negligible share of Korea's total fragrance exports.
KR.trend: The MFDS-sourced 2025 export figure carries a +46.2% observed year-on-year note, off what the source itself calls a small base. No cagr_forecast or domestic-market growth figure is present, so growth direction for the segment beyond exports cannot be assessed from current data.
KR.caveats: No domestic retail or production market size exists for Korea fragrances in the current data - only export values, and those two export figures differ in source, period, and scope (2025 MFDS total vs. 2024 Comtrade HS3303-to-world), so they should not be combined.

IN.read: India fragrances has two RETAIL market-size estimates, both LOW confidence: US$2.6bn (2024) covering perfume plus deodorant combined, and a narrower US$0.281bn (FY24) covering perfume only - different scope, so not directly comparable to each other. Import data is HIGH confidence: India imported US$0.331681bn of fragrances (HS 3303) from the world in 2024, with Korea (US$0.000135bn, [CORRIDOR]-tagged) and China (US$0.000249bn) each a minor source. An ESTIMATE-confidence import-dependence figure of 12.8% notes that premium fragrance is import-reliant (UAE the largest source, then France) while mass-market perfume/deodorant is largely made domestically. A MEDIUM-confidence company figure (Vini Cosmetics/Fogg, FY25 revenue INR 1200cr, NET_REALISATION basis) is also present but reflects one company, not the segment as a whole.
IN.trend: No top-level growth_yoy or cagr_forecast is populated for India fragrances. The notes on both market-size figures do carry forward-looking CAGRs - roughly 11.1% to US$6.7bn by 2033 for the perfume+deodorant estimate, and 15.23% to US$0.873bn by FY2032 for the perfume-only estimate - but both are forecasts, not observed growth, and both come from LOW-confidence sources.
IN.caveats: Both India market-size figures are LOW-confidence industry/aggregator estimates covering different scope (perfume+deodorant vs. perfume-only), so neither should be treated as a single definitive segment size; the 12.8% import-dependence figure is itself labelled ESTIMATE/derived rather than a directly sourced number.

combined.read: A like-for-like comparison of Korea and India fragrances is not possible with the data at hand: Korea's only figures are EXPORT_FOB export values (US$0.06bn in 2025, US$0.039471bn for 2024 world HS3303), while India's are RETAIL market-size estimates (US$2.6bn or US$0.281bn depending on scope) plus IMPORT_CIF figures - different value_basis on both sides, and neither carries a shared value_usd_bn field that would permit direct netting. The Korea-to-India corridor trade flow is present but tiny on both sides of the ledger (KR exports to India US$6,000 in 2024; India imports from Korea US$135,000 in 2024, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged), suggesting fragrances is a minor thread of the broader K-beauty corridor relative to categories like skincare.
